chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the Azan: Is it permissible for it to be from someone who is not knowledgeable? He said: The Azan is not correct, and it is not permissible for it to be recited except by a knowledgeable Muslim man. So if he knows the Azan, he recites it with it; and if he is not knowledgeable, his Azan is not valid, nor is his Iqamah, nor should he be followed (as an Imam).

And he was asked about a man who recites the Azan and Iqamah in order to pray alone, and then another man comes and says to him, 'We should pray in congregation.' Is it permissible for them to pray with that Azan and Iqamah? He said: No, but he should recite an Azan and an Iqamah.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Azan and the ruling when a solitary prayerer is joined by others?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that the validity of the Azan and Iqamah is contingent upon the reciter being an 'Arif' (one knowledgeable of the proper etiquette and conditions), rendering the call of the ignorant invalid for congregational following. The hadith further clarifies the procedural requirement for a new, distinct Azan and Iqamah when a solitary prayer transitions to a congregational one, ensuring the ritual integrity of the communal worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabaty, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

Heasws was asked about the Azān, ‘Is it allowed if it happens to be from someone without understanding?’ Heasws said: ‘No! The Azān is not correct, and it is not allowed that the Azān be recited except by an understanding Muslim man. So if he knows the Azān, so he can recite with it, but if he does not happen to be understanding, his Azān is not allowed, nor is his Iqamah, nor should he be followed with (in the Jam’atal Salāt)’.

And heasws was asked about the man who recites an Azān and an Iqamah in order to pray Salāt alone. So another man comes over and is saying to him, ‘We should pray together’. So is it allowed that he should pray Salāt with that Azān and the Iqamah?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he should recite an Azān and an Iqamah’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about Adhan if one who is not well versed can say Adhan. He (the Imam) said, ‘Adhan does not come right and it is not permissible to say Adhan unless one is a Muslim man and knowledgeable. If he knows Adhan he says it, if he is not well versed it is not permissible for him to say it or ‘Iqamah. One is not permitted to assign him to lead in Salah (prayer).’

He (the Imam) was asked about a man who says Adhan and ‘Iqamah so he can perform Salah (prayer) alone, and then another man comes and says, ‘Allow us to perform Salah (prayer) in congregation.’ Is it permissible that they perform Salah (prayer) with that Adhan and ‘Iqamah?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, but he says Adhan and ‘Iqamah.’”
